entries.title: Hits on a dice pool
entries.summary: Roll a number of d6 equal to your pool. By default, each die showing 5 or 6 is a hit. Some house rules count 4–6 as hits. Net hits are hits after any threshold or opposed hits are subtracted.
entries.formula: Hit on 5–6 (default) · optional house rule: hit on 4–6

entries.title: Glitches and critical glitches
entries.summary: A glitch happens when you roll too many 1s relative to the dice you checked. Edition and house rules choose whether that is more than half or at least half ones. A critical glitch is a glitch with zero hits. ShadowDeck’s roller applies your character’s dice house rules.
entries.formula: Glitch: ones vs pool · Critical: glitch and 0 hits

entries.title: Rule of Six (exploding sixes)
entries.summary: When Rule of Six applies, each 6 is a hit and is rolled again (and can explode again). Core tables usually enable this when spending Edge to push the limit; a house rule can make every 6 explode on every test.
entries.formula: On 6: count hit, roll again (may chain)

entries.title: Push the Limit (Edge before the roll)
entries.summary: Spend Edge before rolling to add your Edge rating in dice and enable Rule of Six on that test (edition- and house-rule dependent). ShadowDeck’s dice roller models this as Push the Limit.
entries.formula: Pool = base + Edge rating; Rule of Six on

entries.title: Second Chance (Edge after the roll)
entries.summary: After seeing the dice, spend Edge to re-roll failed dice (not the 1s that already count toward a glitch, depending on edition procedure). ShadowDeck previews Second Chance from the last roll in the dice inspector.
entries.formula: Re-roll non-hit dice (see book for 1s / Edge cost)

entries.title: Dice house rules in ShadowDeck
entries.summary: Per-character House Rules can change glitch threshold (edition default, more than half, half or more), whether exploded dice count for glitches, hits on 4+, and whether Rule of Six is Edge-only or always on. The roller and glitch calculator read the active character’s resolved dice rules.

entries.title: Opposed tests
entries.summary: Both sides roll. Compare hits; the higher total wins by the difference (net hits). Ties usually favor the defender or produce no effect—check the specific action. Glitches still apply to each side’s roll.
entries.formula: Net hits = attacker hits − defender hits

entries.title: Extended tests (overview)
entries.summary: An extended test accumulates hits over multiple intervals toward a threshold. Each interval is a separate roll of the same pool (often with a rising difficulty or time cost). Use your book for interval length, max rolls, and botch consequences.
entries.formula: Sum hits over intervals ≥ threshold

entries.title: Teamwork tests
entries.summary: Helpers roll first and add some of their hits as dice to the primary actor’s pool (with a cap). Editions differ on who can help and how many bonus dice transfer—use your core book for the exact cap and skill requirements.
entries.formula: Helpers roll → limited hits become bonus dice for the leader

entries.title: Success tests and thresholds
entries.summary: A success test rolls against a threshold or opposed hits. Net hits equal your hits minus the threshold (or defender’s hits). Many actions list a threshold in the book (e.g. climb, perception).
entries.formula: Net hits = hits − threshold (or opposed hits)

entries.title: Buying hits (optional rule)
entries.summary: Some tables allow buying hits instead of rolling when time is short: typically one hit per four dice in the pool (rounded down), with no glitch chance. Confirm your edition’s optional rule before using it.
entries.formula: Often ⌊pool ÷ 4⌋ hits, no roll

entries.title: Building a dice pool
entries.summary: Most pools are skill + linked attribute, plus modifiers (wounds, visibility, gear, spells). Untrained skills often roll attribute −1 or similar. ShadowDeck shows derived pools on the sheet; situational mods go into the roller’s modifier field.
entries.formula: Pool ≈ skill + attribute ± modifiers

entries.title: Defaulting (untrained skills)
entries.summary: When you lack a skill, you may default with the linked attribute at a penalty (commonly −1 die) if the skill allows defaulting. Some skills cannot be defaulted. Check skill lists in your core book.
entries.formula: Often attribute − 1 (if default allowed)

entries.title: Edge refresh and session Edge
entries.summary: Edge rating is a character stat; available Edge is the spendable pool. Refresh timing differs by edition (scene, session, downtime). SR6 emphasizes Edge as a renewable session resource. ShadowDeck tracks Edge for the roller session; permanent Edge changes belong on the sheet.
entries.formula: Spend available Edge; refresh per edition downtime rules

entries.title: Public awareness and notoriety (pointer)
entries.summary: Reputation tracks (street cred, notoriety, public awareness) modify social and legwork tests in some editions. ShadowDeck does not fully automate rep dice—use your book when a contact or Johnson cares who you are.

entries.title: Karma cost to raise a skill
entries.summary: After chargen, raising an active skill by one rank costs karma based on the new rating and edition table. Knowledge and language skills are usually cheaper. ShadowDeck’s Plan tab uses the live edition rules (and soft caps).
entries.formula: SR4/SR5 active: new × 2 · SR6 active: new × 5 · knowledge/language: often new × 1

entries.title: Karma cost to raise an attribute
entries.summary: Raising a natural attribute by one costs karma equal to the new rating times a multiplier (commonly ×5). Metatype maximums still apply. A house rule can switch to a flat cost per step.
entries.formula: Default: new rating × 5 · house rule: flat 5 per step

entries.title: Learning a new skill (rank 0 → 1)
entries.summary: Buying a skill you do not have usually means paying the karma cost for rating 1 under that skill’s category. ShadowDeck’s Plan tab can add a new skill item and apply it when you have the karma.
entries.formula: Cost of raising from 0 → 1 for that category

entries.title: Skill specializations (overview)
entries.summary: A specialization narrows a skill for a bonus on matching tests (commonly +2 dice). Buying or improving specializations costs karma per your edition. ShadowDeck stores a single specialization string per skill instance.
entries.formula: See edition for karma and bonus (often +2 dice)

entries.title: Karma available vs karma total
entries.summary: Karma Total is career karma earned (including what you already spent). Karma Available is the unspent pool you can put into raises. Manual + on Summary awards both; Plan spends reduce available only. Run Apply Awards can credit both with a ledger entry.
entries.formula: Spent ≈ Total − Available (not always exact after imports)

entries.title: Buying qualities after chargen
entries.summary: Positive qualities after play usually cost karma (often double chargen prices). Negative qualities can return karma with GM approval. ShadowDeck’s Qualities tab stores ranks and karma values; legality is between you and your table.
entries.formula: Often 2× chargen karma for positive qualities

entries.title: Initiation and submersion (overview)
entries.summary: Awakened characters initiate; technomancers submerge. Each grade raises Magic or Resonance potential and may grant metamagics or echoes. Costs escalate with grade. ShadowDeck tracks Magic/Resonance ranks—full initiation trees live in the books.
entries.formula: Karma scales with new grade (see edition table)

entries.title: Improving contacts
entries.summary: Raising a contact’s Loyalty or Connection often costs karma or nuyen and fiction time. ShadowDeck stores Loyalty/Connection and favor standing; exact improvement costs are edition- and table-dependent.

entries.title: Knowledge and language advances
entries.summary: Knowledge and language skills usually improve more cheaply than active skills. Some tables treat languages with special ranks (basic/conversational/fluent). Plan tab costs follow edition knowledge multipliers.
entries.formula: Often new rating × 1 karma per rank

entries.title: Martial arts and techniques (pointer)
entries.summary: Martial arts styles and techniques can grant combat options or dice. Costs and prerequisites vary widely by edition supplement. ShadowDeck does not fully encode martial arts trees—track key techniques in notes if needed.

entries.title: Attribute and skill soft caps
entries.summary: Metatype maximums and skill soft caps limit how high ranks can go without special rules. ShadowDeck’s Plan tab respects edition soft caps and metatype ceilings where the rules engine knows them.
entries.formula: Cannot exceed metatype max / skill soft cap without special rules

entries.title: Run awards (nuyen and karma)
entries.summary: Completed runs often award nuyen and karma. ShadowDeck’s Apply Awards splits a run’s payout equally among available linked runners with a confirmation sheet—never automatic on status change.
entries.formula: Equal floor split among available participants

entries.title: Lifestyle levels and monthly cost
entries.summary: Lifestyles abstract housing and living costs. ShadowDeck stores a monthly nuyen cost per lifestyle (user-editable) and offers SR5-oriented suggested amounts for Street through Luxury. Active lifestyles contribute to monthly burn.
entries.formula: Suggested SR5: Street 0 · Squatter 500 · Low 2k · Middle 5k · High 10k · Luxury 100k ¥/mo

entries.title: Process Month (paying lifestyle)
entries.summary: ShadowDeck never auto-charges lifestyle. When you Process Month (1–3 months), prepaid months on each active lifestyle are consumed first; remaining cost pulls from lifestyle reserve, then nuyen. Shortfall blocks the whole action.
entries.formula: Each month: prepaid −1 or pay monthlyCost from reserve then nuyen

entries.title: Lifestyle nuyen reserve
entries.summary: A lifestyle reserve is a buffer spent before liquid nuyen when processing months. You can deposit or withdraw between reserve and nuyen on the Lifestyle tab. It does not replace prepaid months.
entries.formula: Process cost: reserve first, then nuyen

entries.title: Prepaying lifestyle months
entries.summary: You can prepay months on a lifestyle so Process Month burns prepaid counters before cash. Prepay spends nuyen immediately. Useful when a runner will be offline or in the bush.
entries.formula: Pay monthlyCost × months now; store prepaid count

entries.title: Multiple lifestyles
entries.summary: Runners may maintain more than one lifestyle (safehouse + bolt-hole). ShadowDeck sums active lifestyles for monthly burn. Fiction should explain who is covering which site.
entries.formula: Monthly burn = sum of active lifestyle costs

entries.title: Hospitalized and special lifestyles (pointer)
entries.summary: Special lifestyle conditions (hospitalized, identity subscriptions, dependants) appear in some books with extra costs. Model them as extra lifestyle rows or notes when your table uses them.

entries.title: Buying a lifestyle (up-front)
entries.summary: Some editions list a purchase price to establish a lifestyle tier permanently. ShadowDeck focuses on monthly burn tracking; record large buy-ins as nuyen expenses or gear/notes if your table uses them.

entries.title: SINs and lifestyle (pointer)
entries.summary: Fake SINs often include lifestyle coverage or subscriptions. Keep SIN quality separate from lifestyle cost unless your table bundles them. ShadowDeck does not auto-link SINs to lifestyles.

entries.title: Condition monitors (physical and stun)
entries.summary: Physical and stun tracks hold damage boxes. Capacity is derived from Body and Willpower. Filled boxes are play state on the character. Overflow and wound modifiers follow your edition—use the book for death and penalty tables.
entries.formula: Physical = 8 + ⌈Body/2⌉ · Stun = 8 + ⌈Willpower/2⌉

entries.title: SR5 limits (physical, mental, social)
entries.summary: In SR5, limits cap how many hits you can keep on many tests. Physical, Mental, and Social limits are derived from attributes (and essence for social). SR4 and SR6 do not use this limit trio the same way—ShadowDeck only shows SR5 limits on SR5 sheets.
entries.formula: Physical ⌈(STR×2+BOD+REA)/3⌉ · Mental ⌈(LOG×2+INT+WIL)/3⌉ · Social ⌈(CHA×2+WIL+ESS)/3⌉

entries.title: Initiative (score overview)
entries.summary: Initiative score is typically Reaction + Intuition (plus modifiers and initiative dice from gear or magic). Higher goes first; initiative passes and Edge options differ by edition. ShadowDeck shows a base initiative figure on the play sheet—not a multi-domain combat tracker.
entries.formula: Base often REA + INT (+ initiative dice from effects)

entries.title: Action types (overview)
entries.summary: Combat time is built from free, simple, and complex actions (plus interrupts/reactions depending on edition). Exact lists and what you can combine in a pass live in your core book. This card is a pointer only—not a full action encyclopedia.

entries.title: Damage resistance (concept)
entries.summary: After a successful attack, the target usually rolls Body (+ armor, modified by AP) to reduce damage. Net hits left after resistance become boxes on a condition monitor. ShadowDeck tracks armor ratings and monitors but does not fully automate AP vs armor tables yet.
entries.formula: Resist pool ≈ Body + modified armor (see book for AP)

entries.title: Walk and run rates
entries.summary: ShadowDeck’s derived stats use a simple walk/run estimate from Agility for sheet display. Full tactical movement, sprinting, and terrain modifiers belong in your core book and combat tracker workflow.
entries.formula: Display estimate: Walk AGI×2 · Run AGI×4 (meters/turn style guidance)

entries.title: Armor and armor penetration
entries.summary: Armor adds to damage resistance; armor penetration (AP) reduces effective armor (not below zero in most cases). Elemental and DV types may bypass or modify armor. Equip armor on the Gear tab so Summary reflects ratings.
entries.formula: Effective armor ≈ max(0, armor − AP) for that attack

entries.title: Wound modifiers
entries.summary: Filled damage boxes impose dice-pool penalties that grow as you take more damage. Editions differ on the breakpoint tables. ShadowDeck shows filled boxes; apply wound mods manually in the roller until fully automated.
entries.formula: See edition wound table for −dice by boxes filled

entries.title: Recoil compensation
entries.summary: Firing multiple bullets increases recoil. Compensation from strength, stock, and accessories reduces the penalty. Exact progressive recoil math is edition-specific—use the firearm chapter for full auto and burst rules.
entries.formula: Uncompensated recoil → dice penalty (see edition)

entries.title: Cover and visibility
entries.summary: Cover can add dice to defense or impose attack penalties; visibility and range modifiers stack. ShadowDeck does not simulate battle maps—apply situational mods in the dice roller.

entries.title: Defense tests
entries.summary: Defenders typically roll Reaction (+ Intuition) plus modifiers against the attacker’s hits. Full defense and interrupt actions may raise the pool or cost actions. Net hits determine whether the attack lands and how hard.
entries.formula: Defense pool ≈ REA (+ INT) ± mods

entries.title: Surprise
entries.summary: Surprised characters may lose actions or defend poorly at the start of combat. Perception and ambush setup matter. Resolve surprise with your book before the first initiative pass.

entries.title: Called shots (overview)
entries.summary: Called shots trade dice penalties (or Edge) for special effects: disable a limb, bypass armor, trick shot, etc. Lists differ by edition. Not automated in ShadowDeck—apply the listed penalty in the roller.
entries.formula: Attack pool − called-shot penalty (see list)

entries.title: Melee combat (overview)
entries.summary: Melee uses close-combat skills plus Strength or Agility depending on edition and weapon. Reach, charging, and multiple opponents have special rules. Use the combat chapter for grappling and martial arts.

entries.title: Grenades and blast (pointer)
entries.summary: Grenades use throw tests and blast damage with distance falloff. Deviations on misses can endanger friends. Model damage on condition monitors after book resolution.

entries.title: Vehicle combat (pointer)
entries.summary: Vehicle combat uses handling, speed, and sensor tests with chase and ramming options. ShadowDeck is not a full chase engine—use the book and track vehicle condition in notes if needed.

entries.title: Drain (spellcasting)
entries.summary: Casting a spell causes Drain equal to a Force-based code (for example F/2+2). You resist Drain with Willpower plus your tradition attribute. This card’s calculator is a quick aid—traditions, reagents, overcasting, and full tables live in your core book.
entries.formula: DV from Force code · Resist WIL + tradition attribute

entries.title: Spell Force
entries.summary: Force sets a spell’s power, range, and Drain code. You cannot usually cast above your Magic attribute without overcasting rules. Higher Force means harder Drain and stronger effects.
entries.formula: Force ≤ Magic (without overcast rules)

entries.title: Traditions and Drain attributes
entries.summary: A tradition pairs Magic with a Drain attribute (e.g. Logic, Charisma, Intuition). It also colors spirits and roleplay. ShadowDeck stores tradition name; Drain calculator lets you pick the attribute.
entries.formula: Drain resist = WIL + tradition attribute

entries.title: Summoning spirits (overview)
entries.summary: Summoning rolls Magic + summoning skill against the spirit’s Force; Drain follows. Services and binding are separate steps. ShadowDeck is not a full spirit manager—track spirit Force and services in notes if needed.
entries.formula: Opposed Magic + skill vs Force; then Drain

entries.title: Spirits and services
entries.summary: Spirits have Force-based attributes and powers. Services are spent for combat, powers, or remote tasks. Banishing opposes the spirit. Exact type lists are edition-specific.

entries.title: Adept powers (overview)
entries.summary: Adepts spend Power Points (usually equal to Magic) on powers that enhance combat, stealth, or social edges. ShadowDeck’s Magic tab tracks adept powers and can apply sheet modifiers when powers include mechanical bonuses.
entries.formula: Power Points ≈ Magic (before initiation losses)

entries.title: Foci and bonding
entries.summary: Foci add dice or sustain spells but cost karma to bond and can be turned against you. Force and type matter for availability and addiction risks in some editions. Track bonded foci as gear with notes.
entries.formula: Bonding karma often scales with Force

entries.title: Reagents (overview)
entries.summary: Reagents can lower Drain, assist alchemy, or enable ritual work. Units and purity rules vary. ShadowDeck does not inventory reagents automatically—note stocks if your campaign tracks them.

entries.title: Alchemy and preparations (pointer)
entries.summary: Alchemy creates preparations that release spell effects later. Potency, lynchpins, and command words are book systems. Use Magic notes for prepared items.

entries.title: Astral perception and projection
entries.summary: Astral perception lets you see auras; projection leaves the body vulnerable. Dual-natured threats and wards matter. Combat on the astral uses different attributes—see the astral combat section of your book.

entries.title: Wards and magical security (pointer)
entries.summary: Wards block or alert on astral intrusion. Force and type determine resistance. Corporate sites lean heavily on wards—plan legwork accordingly.

entries.title: Background count (pointer)
entries.summary: Background count can raise or lower effective Magic and Drain in corrupted or sacred sites. Apply as a situational Magic modifier when the GM declares a count.
entries.formula: Often ± count to Magic / Drain difficulty

entries.title: Counterspelling
entries.summary: Counterspelling adds dice to resist spells or can dispel sustained effects. Declare defense when you are aware of hostile magic. Pool uses Counterspelling skill + Magic.
entries.formula: Defense: Counterspelling + Magic (see book)

entries.title: Overwatch Score (overview)
entries.summary: Illegal or noisy Matrix actions accumulate Overwatch Score. When OS hits the convergence threshold, GOD comes looking. ShadowDeck’s calculator uses a simplified action cost table for session tracking—not a full Matrix resolution engine.
entries.formula: OS += action cost · Convergence often ~40 (edition-dependent)

entries.title: Personas and icons
entries.summary: Your persona is your Matrix self; devices and hosts appear as icons. Attack, Sleaze, Data Processing, and Firewall (or edition equivalents) define cybercombat and stealth. ShadowDeck stores decker gear but does not simulate hosts.

entries.title: Noise and signal
entries.summary: Noise from distance, spam, and jamming reduces Matrix dice pools. Sharing and data taps can help. Apply noise as a negative modifier when the GM declares it.
entries.formula: Matrix pool − noise (min 0)

entries.title: Cybercombat (overview)
entries.summary: Cybercombat pits Attack vs Firewall (and similar) with digital damage tracks. Programs and agent help. Convergence and link-locking end poorly for the decker.

entries.title: Sleaze and running silent
entries.summary: Sleaze actions hide your icon or invade quietly. Running silent makes you harder to spot but can impede your own perception. Failed stealth raises OS or alerts hosts.

entries.title: Hosts and IC (pointer)
entries.summary: Hosts have ratings, IC, and security spiders. Brute-forcing or social-engineering entry are both valid. ShadowDeck is not a host generator—use published hosts or GM notes.

entries.title: Technomancers and Resonance
entries.summary: Technomancers use Resonance instead of cyberdecks, with complex forms and sprites. Fading is their Drain analog. Submersion improves Resonance potential.
entries.formula: Fading similar to Drain structure

entries.title: Rigging and RCCs (pointer)
entries.summary: Riggers jump into drones and vehicles via RCCs and control rigs. Noise, sharing, and initiative in the machine matter. Track drones as gear; resolve jumped-in combat with the book.

entries.title: Marks (overview)
entries.summary: Marks represent illegal access on an icon. More marks enable stronger actions (edit, crash, reboot). Gaining marks is often an Attack or Sleaze test vs the target’s defenses.

entries.title: Programs and agents
entries.summary: Common programs (Encryption, Biofeedback Filter, etc.) and agents automate tasks. Running too many programs can tax Data Processing. List key programs on your deck gear notes.

entries.title: Social tests and etiquette
entries.summary: Social skills (Etiquette, Negotiation, Con, Intimidation, Leadership) plus Charisma drive most interpersonal tests. Glitches can offend powerful people. Apply situational mods for culture, prejudice, and attire.
entries.formula: Pool ≈ social skill + CHA ± mods

entries.title: Negotiation and opposed social
entries.summary: Negotiation is often opposed (your Negotiation vs their Negotiation or Willpower+Charisma). Net hits shift price, terms, or attitude. Bring leverage as dice or thresholds.
entries.formula: Opposed social skill tests; net hits = leverage

entries.title: Contacts (Loyalty and Connection)
entries.summary: Loyalty measures how far a contact will go for you; Connection measures their reach. ShadowDeck stores both plus tags, favors, and an interaction log. Improve them with karma, nuyen, and fiction.

entries.title: Favors and chips
entries.summary: Contacts owe or collect favors. ShadowDeck’s favor standing and log help track who is up. Spending a favor can remove dice penalties or open doors—GM fiat still rules outcomes.

entries.title: Leadership and teamwork social
entries.summary: Leadership can coordinate teams, inspire, and sometimes grant teamwork benefits. Use it for crew briefings and NPC management mid-run.

entries.title: Intimidation
entries.summary: Intimidation forces compliance through fear. It can backfire into lasting enmity. Opposed by Willpower-linked defenses or Intimidation.

entries.title: Con and disguise social
entries.summary: Con covers fast-talk and scams; disguise and forgery support false identities. Opposed by Judge Intentions / Perception-style defenses depending on edition.

entries.title: Judge Intentions
entries.summary: Judge Intentions (or similar) pits your social perception against the target’s composure to sense honesty or mood. Useful before deals and ambushes.
entries.formula: Often CHA + skill vs WIL + skill

entries.title: Priority chargen (overview)
entries.summary: SR5 and SR6 default chargen assign A–E priorities to metatype, attributes, magic/resonance, skills, and resources. ShadowDeck’s wizard enforces the selected edition’s priority table and house-rule variants (e.g. Sum-to-Ten).

entries.title: Karma generation (overview)
entries.summary: Some tables use pure karma build instead of priorities. Point totals and freebies differ by house rule pack. ShadowDeck’s primary path is priority/wizard; karma gen is a table agreement.

entries.title: Metatype choice
entries.summary: Metatype sets attribute minimums/maximums and special qualities (low-light, reach, etc.). Priority or BP cost reflects how strong the metatype is. ShadowDeck applies metatype attribute bounds in the wizard and validation.

entries.title: Qualities at chargen
entries.summary: Positive qualities cost build resources; negative qualities return resources with roleplay hooks. Essence, karma, and availability limits apply. ShadowDeck’s Qualities tab and catalog browser support selection.

entries.title: Resources and nuyen at start
entries.summary: Resources priority (or BP) becomes starting nuyen for gear. Leftover cash may convert to lifestyle or carry into play per table rules. ShadowDeck sets starting nuyen from the wizard resources step.

entries.title: Magic / Resonance at chargen
entries.summary: Magic or Resonance priority grants Magician, Adept, Technomancer, etc., with a starting Magic/Resonance rank and skills. Mundanes skip this column. ShadowDeck’s wizard branches on the chosen path.

entries.title: Skill ranks at chargen
entries.summary: Skill points or skill priorities buy ranks and groups. Specializations may be free or cheap at chargen. ShadowDeck’s wizard allocates skill ranks per edition method.

entries.title: Attributes at chargen
entries.summary: Attribute points raise stats within metatype limits. Special attributes (Edge, Magic, Resonance) follow separate budgets. Validation catches illegal arrays.

entries.title: Essence and cyberware at chargen
entries.summary: Cyberware and bioware cost Essence and nuyen. Magic users lose maximum Magic as Essence drops. ShadowDeck tracks Essence on augs and validates Magic caps.
entries.formula: Essence starts at 6; augs reduce it

entries.title: Knowledge skills at chargen
entries.summary: Knowledge and language points are often free formulas from attributes (e.g. Logic/Intuition based). House rules may grant free knowledge ranks. ShadowDeck supports free-knowledge house rules where implemented.
entries.formula: Often free points from LOG / INT formulas

entries.title: Starting contacts
entries.summary: Chargen may grant free contact points (CHA-based) to buy Loyalty and Connection. ShadowDeck’s contact tools work the same after play begins.
entries.formula: Often free contact points ≈ CHA × N

entries.title: Final touches and playability
entries.summary: Before play, confirm lifestyle, SIN, commlink, and a way to receive jobs. ShadowDeck’s validation banner flags empty skills, zero Edge issues, and other sheet problems.

entries.title: Gear ratings and availability
entries.summary: Gear has rating, availability, and cost. Restricted items need licenses or black-market channels. ShadowDeck’s catalog browser lists bundled SR5 stats; custom gear is always allowed.

entries.title: Weapons and damage codes
entries.summary: Weapons list DV, AP, mode, and ammo. Skill and specialization govern the attack pool. Equip weapons on the Gear tab so armor and bonuses update the sheet.

entries.title: Armor pieces and capacity
entries.summary: Armor provides rating and often capacity for modifications. Stacking rules prevent infinite armor. ShadowDeck uses equipped armor ratings for Summary armor display.

entries.title: Cyberware grades
entries.summary: Standard, alpha, beta, and delta grades change Essence cost and price. Used cyberware may be cheaper and riskier. ShadowDeck stores grade and Essence on augmentation rows.

entries.title: Bioware
entries.summary: Bioware costs Essence (often less harshly than cyber) and nuyen, with culturing time in fiction. Track implanted bioware on the Augs tab.

entries.title: Commlinks and decks
entries.summary: Commlinks provide Matrix attributes for everyday users; cyberdecks power deckers. Device rating and programs matter. Store devices as gear with notes for ASDF arrays.

entries.title: Vehicles and drones
entries.summary: Vehicles list handling, speed, body, armor, and pilot. Drones need pilots or jumped-in riggers. ShadowDeck can store them as gear; combat uses book vehicle rules.

entries.title: Ammunition types
entries.summary: Ammo variants change DV, AP, or special effects (gel, APDS, explosive). Track loaded ammo in notes if your table is strict about counts.

entries.title: Drugs and toxins (pointer)
entries.summary: Drugs grant short bonuses with addiction and side effects. Toxins use vector and power. Resolve with the toxin chapter; record doses in gear or notes.

entries.title: Essence loss and Magic
entries.summary: As Essence falls, maximum Magic/Resonance usually falls. Adepts and magicians must plan ware carefully. ShadowDeck validation warns when Magic exceeds Essence-based maximums where known.
entries.formula: Max Magic often ≤ ⌈Essence⌉ (see edition)

entries.title: Playing glitches at the table
entries.summary: Mechanical glitches are an invitation for complication, not automatic failure of the whole mission. Critical glitches should sting without ending the campaign unless the fiction demands it.

entries.title: House rules philosophy
entries.summary: ShadowDeck’s House Rules browser toggles popular mechanical variants (Sum-to-Ten, dice, free knowledge, etc.). Keep the list short so the table remembers what is on. Custom fiction rules stay in notes.

entries.title: Legwork and matrix search
entries.summary: Legwork combines social contacts, Matrix search, and knowledge skills. Extended tests and teamwork often apply. Use dice cards for the rolls; use contacts for the fiction pipeline.

entries.title: Heat and consequences
entries.summary: Runs generate heat that can raise security, close contacts, or attract hunters. ShadowDeck’s Run tracker records heat fields—apply fiction fallout on the next job.

entries.title: Downtime between runs
entries.summary: Downtime is for healing, training, lifestyle, and side hustles. ShadowDeck’s Process Month, Plan tab, and contact logs are the mechanical hooks—schedule fiction between sessions.

entries.title: Healing and recovery (overview)
entries.summary: Stun heals faster than physical; medicine and magic can accelerate recovery. Overflow and permanent damage rules are edition-specific. Clear boxes on the condition track when the book says you recover.

entries.title: Perception tests
entries.summary: Perception (or similar) notices details, ambushes, and Matrix icons. Thresholds rise with distance and distraction. Team perception can use teamwork rules.
entries.formula: Pool ≈ Perception + INT ± mods

entries.title: Sneaking and infiltration
entries.summary: Sneaking is opposed by Perception. Cameras, magic, and noise change the contest. Matrix silent running is the digital cousin.
entries.formula: Sneaking + AGI vs Perception + INT (typical)

entries.title: Survival and environment
entries.summary: Survival covers weather, wilderness, and toxic zones. Extended tests and gear (breathers, survival kits) matter. Apply environmental wound or fatigue rules from the book.

entries.title: Subculture etiquette
entries.summary: Etiquette specializations (street, corporate, magic, Matrix) can grant bonuses when you speak the right language of power. Wrong scene, wrong clothes—take penalties.
